# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is a book about two things at once: **who the best footballers of the last
twenty-five years were**, and **how you would actually find out**.

## The answer, before the argument

No suspense. Here is what the method produces, computed live from the same data
every chapter uses. A player must clear a floor on **all eleven requirements**
to appear at all.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd

ranking = pd.read_parquet("data/sample/ranking.parquet")
keepers = pd.read_parquet("data/sample/keeper_ranking.parquet")
offsets = pd.read_parquet("data/sample/league_offsets.parquet")

mean, spread = ranking["score"].mean(), ranking["score"].std()
best = ranking[ranking["qualified"]].head(10).copy()
best.insert(0, "#", range(1, len(best) + 1))
best["σ above mean"] = ((best["score"] - mean) / spread).round(1)
best[["#", "player", "score", "σ above mean", "seasons", "leagues"]].round(2).style.hide(axis="index")
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
from IPython.display import Markdown

qualified = int(ranking["qualified"].sum())
kq = keepers[keepers["qualified"]]
Markdown(
    f"**{qualified} of {len(ranking):,} players** clear every requirement. "
    f"Goalkeepers are ranked separately on their own eight requirements: "
    f"{', '.join(kq.head(5)['player'])}. Save percentage and goals per 90 "
    f"are not comparable quantities and pretending otherwise would be dishonest.\n\n"
    f"League strength is estimated from transfers alone, with England pinned at zero: "
    + ", ".join(
        f"**{lg.split('-')[0]}** {v:+.3f}"
        for lg, v in offsets.groupby("league")["offset"].mean().sort_values(ascending=False).items()
    )
    + "."
)
```

**Now the part that matters.** That table is an ordering, and the statistics
behind it do not support one: only three of the twenty-eight pairs among the top
eight can be told apart at all. Chapters 6 and 7 make that case against the
table above, which is the honest way round.

Those two questions are harder to separate than they look. Most arguments about
the greatest player are not really disagreements about facts. They are
disagreements about what "greatest" means, conducted as though they were
disagreements about facts. One person means peak. Another means longevity.
A third means trophies. They talk past each other for hours and nobody moves.

So this book does the unglamorous thing first: it says out loud what it is
measuring, shows you the arithmetic, and tells you where the arithmetic runs out.

## Two ways to read this

**If you are learning data science**, read the investigation chapters in order.
They move from a raw table of numbers to a defended conclusion, and every time a
statistical idea is needed, it appears with a link to the chapter that derives
it properly. You can follow the story without clicking a single one of those
links, and you will still know what was done and why.

**If you already know the statistics**, the method chapters are the substance.
Each follows the same six-part structure:

> **Question → Intuition → Math → Code → Assumptions → How it breaks**

That last section is the one most tutorials skip, and it is the one that matters
most. Any method looks good on the data it was demonstrated with.

## What this project honestly cannot do

Being clear about limits early is not modesty, it is what makes the rest
trustworthy.

- **Advanced statistics do not exist before 2017-18.** Expected goals,
  progressive passes, shot-creating actions: none of it was recorded for the
  2003-04 season, by anyone, at any price. So the ranking here is built on what
  *is* measurable across the whole period: goals, assists, minutes, and the
  strength of the opposition. Richer 2017-onward data appears only as context,
  never as part of the ranking, because a metric that exists for one era and not
  another cannot fairly compare them.
- **This covers the Big 5 domestic leagues**, 2000-01 to 2024-25: England,
  Spain, Italy, Germany and France. No Champions League, no internationals, no
  league outside those five. A player who did their best work in Portugal or
  Brazil does not appear, and that is a limitation of scope, not a judgement.
- **Attacking output is not all of football.** The current rating rewards goals
  and assists. It therefore systematically undervalues defenders and holding
  midfielders. This is stated plainly rather than buried, because a reader who
  does not know it would draw wrong conclusions from an otherwise correct
  calculation.

## Reproducing everything

Every figure in this book is generated by code that runs against a small
committed dataset, so you can re-run the whole thing without scraping anything:

```bash
uv sync --all-groups
uv run pytest
quarto render
```

To rebuild the underlying data from source instead, see `DATA_SOURCES.md` for
the terms each provider imposes, and run `uv run gambeta all`.
